title: Three-phase upgrade: London planning evidence
question: What is the highest and lowest a TPI can charge for a three-phase upgrade?
answer: Assuming a London home or small-business site, the local contractor guide gives £3,000–£8,000 as an indicative total upgrade budget. Its specific upgrade-plus-new-board package starts at £4,995. These are underlying-works contractor examples, not verified lowest/highest broker fees. VAT is not stated; confirm the scope and any separate TPI fee in an itemised quote. Complex projects can exceed the guide range.
default_assumption: London, small commercial premises, existing single-phase electricity supply upgraded to three-phase, with a basic distribution-board replacement. This is an explicit planning assumption, not a known site specification.

broker_fee.status: No fixed public fee found on previously reviewed broker pages
broker_fee.context: Underlying network and electrical works are not an energy broker's administration fee. A missing public fee is not £0. Energy-contract commission is also separate. See tools/tpi-research.json for the eight-broker evidence reviewed on the same date.

budgets.job: Single-to-three-phase upgrade, straightforward small commercial unit
budgets.area: London planning proxy from a UK commercial contractor guide
budgets.basis: Oleco's July 2026 commercial guide gives £1,500–£4,000 for straightforward DNO works with three-phase available at the street and a short service cable, plus £2,000–£5,000 for a small unit's basic three-phase board and circuit redistribution. Adding those component endpoints gives £3,500–£9,000. This sum is our calculation, not a quoted package price.
budgets.context: UK guide used unchanged as an initial London budget. No London uplift invented. Supplier metering charges and any broker arrangement fee are extra and unknown; full rewiring, extensive sub-distribution, major civil works or network reinforcement fall outside this straightforward scenario. This range is not a verified market minimum or maximum.
budgets.vat: VAT inclusion is not stated by the guide. Confirm before quoting a VAT-inclusive or ex-VAT total.

network_scope: UKPN offers single-to-three-phase upgrades up to 70kVA for homes and small businesses. Its current official cost page offers an interactive cost indicator, not a numeric market band. Larger commercial supplies require a specific assessment. Source: https://www.ukpowernetworks.co.uk/i-already-have-electricity-domestic/adding-more-power/what-do-you-need-to-upgrade
metering_scope: A supplier owns the electricity meter; DNO works and metering must be coordinated. Octopus' no-charge standard-metering claim is on a domestic page and must not be automatically applied to businesses. Business meter charges must be confirmed with the relevant supplier.
methodology: Live primary provider pages checked 1 October 2026. Contractor guide ranges are planning estimates, not audited transaction data. London evidence is corroborative only; no numerical highest/lowest broker fee has been invented. Show a useful budget even when exact broker fees are unavailable, and clearly separate the unknown fee from the estimated underlying works.

londonEstimate.customer: Home or small business; confirm package scope
londonEstimate.basis: Electrician247.London publishes £3,000–£8,000 as a realistic total depending on dig length, cable upgrade and metering arrangement. Its separate priced package for a single-to-three-phase DNO upgrade plus new board starts at £4,995 and lists DNO application, dig, cable, new metering and TP&N board. The narrative range and advertised package are distinct examples, not a fixed tariff.
londonEstimate.context: Provisional London planning estimate, not a confirmed market minimum or maximum. The provider works with homes and small commercial sites. Confirm exact network, supplier-metering, internal-board and broker-arrangement inclusions in an itemised quote. A TPI fee is separate and unpublished; do not invent it or call it £0. Complex reinforcement or civil works can exceed this guide range.
londonEstimate.vat: VAT basis not stated on the contractor page; confirm with the provider.
